summary: Kickoff for Aurora Health Redwood onboarding. Covered high-level rollout plan, SSO/SAML, VPC/private deployment options, KMS and data residency, Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, pilot acceptance criteria, and immediate action items to provision test capacity and share security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Uh quick intro, Ethan is our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Ethan Chen: Hi all, hey, hi, glad to be here.
[00:18] Dr. Lisa Moore: Hi, Lisa here. Jamal, Priya, Riley are on as well.
[00:25] Maya Patel: Great, agenda for today: kickoff goals, roles, timeline for pilot, security and network needs, and next steps. We'll keep it tight to 45 minutes.
[00:37] Riley Adams: Sounds good. We're hoping to get a pilot running in 2-3 weeks if possible.
[00:45] Jamal Rivera: Yeah, our main blockers are SSO integration and having a test VPC for the private deployment — also cost targets.
[00:52] Maya Patel: Understood. Quick question on compliance: Priya, what do you need from us up-front?
[00:58] Priya Nair: SOC 2 Type II cert, ISO docs, details on audit logs retention, and KMS integration notes. Also a short rundown of data residency and encryption in transit and at rest.
[01:12] Ethan Chen: We can share the SOC 2 report and our security package after the call; notes on KMS — Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and we can document rotation and access controls.
[01:28] Priya Nair: Okay, we need the KMS rotation policy by next week ideally.
[01:34] Maya Patel: Noted.
[01:36] Ethan Chen: On the deployment side, two paths: Hosted API for fastest time-to-value, or Redwood Dedicated / Private for VPC and on-prem needs. For PHI workloads you mentioned, Private with a customer VPC or on-prem is an option.
[01:53] Dr. Lisa Moore: We will have PHI — so private is likely. Can you explain networking implications?
[02:00] Ethan Chen: Sure — for Private we deploy a control plane managed by Redwood but the inference plane sits in your VPC. We support cross-account VPC peering or use Transit Gateway depending on cloud. There are firewall rules and minimal outbound allowed ports.
[02:18] Riley Adams: Any special NAT or egress controls? Our security team is strict.
[02:22] Ethan Chen: We can work with your cloud infra — typically only outbound to Redwood's control-plane endpoints on port 443 for metrics and control; customer data stays in your VPC/regions.
[02:35] Jamal Rivera: Performance wise, what's the process for model versions and rollouts? We don't want noisy deploys affecting latency.
[02:42] Ethan Chen: We do canary and A/B rollouts. Dedicated pools let you pin instances to a model version, and our runtime supports KV cache and continuous batching so cold starts are minimized. For latency SLOs you can set routing policies and have fallback to a smaller lower-cost model variant.
[03:05] Maya Patel: Jamal also asked about cost tradeoffs — Ethan, quick summary?
[03:10] Ethan Chen: Hosted is pay-as-you-go — easiest but less isolation. Dedicated is reserved capacity, better unit economics at steady QPS. Private has overhead for network and KMS but required for compliance. Batching and prefix cache reduce per-token cost, and we provide Optimize recommendations for quantization.
[03:33] Dr. Lisa Moore: We saw references to KV cache in the docs — is that safe for PHI?
[03:40] Ethan Chen: The KV cache is managed within the inference plane; in Private deployment it stays inside your VPC and doesn't leave. You can configure cache retention and flush policies, and we can disable persistent caching if you require no caching.
[03:57] Priya Nair: Need that documented. Also, audit logs: can you provide token-level logging granularities? We need to know what we can retain and anonymize.
[04:08] Ethan Chen: Yes, you get per-request metadata, response times, and token counts. For Private we can ship logs to your CloudWatch/Splunk/S3 — retention configurable.
[04:20] Riley Adams: Ok, pilot acceptance criteria — what do you usually see?
[04:25] Maya Patel: Typically functional correctness on a subset of prompts, latency under agreed SLO (p90), and throughput targets for your peak. Also integration success for SSO and KMS.
[04:36] Jamal Rivera: We'll aim for p90 < 250ms for simple completions, but that's a starting point.
[04:44] Ethan Chen: For sequence lengths and model choice that will vary, we should run a small benchmark with your sample traces.
[04:53] Dr. Lisa Moore: We'll share sample traces and expected QPS.
[04:57] Jamal Rivera: Yeah, we can extract a week of inference logs and anonymize.
[05:03] Maya Patel: Perfect. So immediate items: we'll send SOC2 and security packet, and Ethan will provision a test Dedicated environment while we finalize Private networking.
[05:15] Priya Nair: One more — SSO. We use Okta. What's the flow and is SAML supported?
[05:22] Ethan Chen: Yes, SAML/Okta supported. We have an integration guide; you'll upload the IdP metadata and we provide SP metadata. We also support SCIM for user provisioning.
[05:34] Priya Nair: SCIM is important for us.
[05:38] Ethan Chen: Noted.
[05:40] Riley Adams: Onboarding timeline — who owns what?
[05:44] Maya Patel: I'll own overall project and pricing; Ethan will own technical setup and work with Jamal; Priya will validate security artifacts; Riley will validate product acceptance.
[05:56] Dr. Lisa Moore: Rough timeline: week 1 security review + test env, week 2 run benchmarks + integration, week 3 pilot evaluation. Is that feasible?
[06:05] Ethan Chen: That seems reasonable; provisioning Dedicated test nodes can happen in 2-3 business days after we get an account and some minimal info.
[06:14] Jamal Rivera: What's minimal info?
[06:16] Ethan Chen: Cloud account ID, VPC/subnet IDs for Private, PKI or KMS details if using customer-managed keys, and a service account for us to provision resources or instructions for cross-account role.
[06:30] Jamal Rivera: I'll follow up with a checklist.
[06:33] Maya Patel: We'll send a short onboarding checklist after the call.
[06:37] [07:00] Maya Patel: Some notes on pricing — for Dedicated we'll share reserved commit tiers; pilot usually uses short-term commit/discounts.
[07:08] Dr. Lisa Moore: Any per-token pricing differences for quantized models?
[07:12] Ethan Chen: Quantized variants reduce memory and GPU cost; we price by effective compute units and tokens — we'll include quantization recommendations in the Optimize report.
[07:26] Riley Adams: Security question — where are keys stored? KMS or do you manage keys?
[07:31] Ethan Chen: For Private, you can supply your KMS keys; Redwood can also manage keys but for PHI customers we recommend customer-managed KMS.
[07:41] Priya Nair: We will insist on customer-managed keys.
[07:44] Ethan Chen: Understood. We'll include KMS steps in the network workshop.
[07:50] Maya Patel: Ok, let's talk about observability — what dashboards will you get?
[07:55] Ethan Chen: Redwood Console will show token-level cost, per-route latency, tracing hooks, and error rates. You can export metrics to your monitoring stack.
[08:06] Riley Adams: Can we get per-model dashboards for A/B tests?
[08:09] Ethan Chen: Yes, per-model/per-route dashboards and rollout controls.
[08:14] Dr. Lisa Moore: For the pilot we'll want a canary to compare the new model to our current baseline.
[08:20] Ethan Chen: We can set up canary rollouts and automated rollback if quality drops.
[08:26] Maya Patel: Any other questions on security or network?
[08:29] Priya Nair: Data residency — we need to ensure logs and backups are kept in region.
[08:34] Ethan Chen: Private deployment keeps data in your cloud region; logs can be routed to your regional bucket.
[08:40] Jamal Rivera: Great.
[08:42] Maya Patel: Ok, next concrete steps — I'll send the SOC2 and onboarding checklist today, Maya will also share pricing, Ethan will provision test Dedicated environment and schedule a technical workshop with Jamal, Priya to review KMS docs.
[09:00] Riley Adams: Can we target the tech workshop for next Wednesday?
[09:05] Ethan Chen: I have availability then; I'll send a calendar invite after the call.
[09:10] Dr. Lisa Moore: Good.
[09:12] Maya Patel: Any blockers from anyone?
[09:15] Priya Nair: No blockers, just need the docs.
[09:18] Jamal Rivera: I'll prepare the sample traces.
[09:21] Maya Patel: Great. Quick recap: send docs, provision test env, schedule workshop, share checklist and finalize pilot criteria.
[09:33] Riley Adams: Thanks everyone.
[09:36] Maya Patel: Thanks, we'll follow up with notes and action items.
[09:40] [End at 15:46 UTC]
